record.question: What happens when data acquisition in K-space does not cover the outer edges (high spatial frequencies) sufficiently?
options: The image will appear completely black.
The image will have reduced spatial resolution (blurriness).
The image will have decreased signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
The image contrast will be reversed.
record.explanation: Answer B: The image will have reduced spatial resolution (blurriness).. Omitting outer k-space/high spatial-frequency data blurs fine detail and lowers spatial resolution. Reference: https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/mri; https://cs.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/Radiology-Safety/MR-Safety/Manual-on-MR-Safety.pdf. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
